κήρ-ωμα , ατος, τό,
A. = κηρωτή , wax-salve, cerate, Hp. Acut.(Sp.) 15 , 33 (both pl.), Orib. Fr. 63 (pl.).
2. layer of mud or clay forming the floor of the wrestling-ring in the times of the Empire, Lat. ceroma, locus exercitii utilis . . aequali et molli ceromate stratus, Cael.Aur. Salut.Praec. 35 (ed.V.Rose Anecd.Gr. 2.199 ), cf. Plu. 2.638c , Plin. HN 35.168 , Mart. 4.19.5 , al.; a ceromate nos haphe excepit, out of the mud into the dust, Sen. Ep. 57.1 : metaph. for the wrestling-ring or wrestling, “ἐν παλαίστραις καὶ κηρώμασι”
Plu. 2.790f
, cf. Plin. HN 35.5 .
3. waxed tablet or board,
IG 7.413.59 ( S. C. de Orop.).
From A Greek-English Lexicon (Henry George Liddell, Robert Scott, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1940)
